messages:
incident-bot: PAGERS: Inference cluster (infer-usw) seeing elevated errors and latency. Route: infer-pool-1. Auto-escalating to on-call Maya Patel. Please ack. https://incidents.internal/4449873210 :rotating_light:
Maya Patel: acked, I'm on it. seeing a flurry of NotReady events and kubelet restarts across infer-usw-3/4/5. pulling logs now.
Maya Patel: quick snippet from node logs:
```
May 06 12:03:12 infer-usw-3 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
May 06 12:03:13 containerd: shim reaped for pod inference-worker-abc: exit code 137
May 06 12:03:14 kubelet: NodeStatus transition NotReady -> Ready -> NotReady (restarts)
```
Jon Liu: omg 137 + Xid 79 usually points at driver/firmware or sudden GPU reset. any recent driver rollouts to those nodes?
Maya Patel: no driver rollout in last 24h, but infra-bot shows a host reboot batch ~2h ago on the same AZ. suspect memory leak / nv driver instability.
Sophia Ramirez: +1 on driver suspicion. i saw similar with 530.x on some test clusters — the kernel + driver combo caused MMU faults over long-lived workloads.
Alice Chen: customers: routing telemetry shows ~4% of requests hitting infer-usw failing with 5xx and 99th latency spiking to 3.2s. top-affected models are small-gpt-quant and reranker-v1.
Maya Patel: mitigation plan: 1) cordon/drain bad nodes, 2) disable continuous batching on gateway for live traffic to reduce memory pressure, 3) shift traffic weight to infer-eu while we stabilize. executing now.
Jon Liu: commands to run (copy/paste):
```
kubectl cordon infer-usw-3
kubectl drain infer-usw-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
# scale fallback pool
kubectl scale deployment infer-gateway -n inference --replicas=10
```
Maya Patel: running cordon+drain on 3/4/5. draining 3 -> evicting pods now. patching route weights to reduce USW to 30%: infra-bot executing trafficctl change.
infra-bot: trafficctl: applied weights: infer-usw=30 infer-eu=70. Rolling update to gateway replicas in progress.
Sophia Ramirez: also toggle runtime flag to reduce batch size for small-gpt-quant (will drop throughput but reduce per-pod memory):
```
curl -XPOST https://runtime.internal/flags -d '{"model":"small-gpt-quant","batch_size":8}'
```
Maya Patel: done toggling batch_size -> 8. Observing memory usage falling on remaining nodes. GPU OOMs dropping.
Alice Chen: customer-facing note: hitting ~2% 5xx after mitigation; major traffic paths recovered. open incident ticket INC-1453, setting Sev2 for now.
Jon Liu: can we put a temporary node selector to avoid nodes with older kernel? label suggestion: node.k8s.redwood/driver-version=530-broken -> taint?
Maya Patel: good call — adding taint to isolate older-driver nodes and adding new nodes with validated driver version.
Maya Patel: taint command:
```
kubectl taint nodes infer-usw-3 node.k8s.redwood/driver=legacy:NoSchedule
```
Sophia Ramirez: i'll prepare a canary driver rollout to roll forward to 535.x on a single node to see if resets stop. recommend keeping 2 nodes warm in eu to absorb traffic until we validate.
Alice Chen: notifying affected customers via status page draft: "We experienced increased errors and latency due to node-level GPU resets in our US-West inference pool. We’ve reduced traffic to the region and are investigating a driver-related root cause. No data loss reported."
Maya Patel: handoff plan: i'll stay on until the eu pool reaches steady-state (30m blocks). then daytime SRE (Jon) will take over post-handoff. will collect kubelet logs and nvml traces for postmortem.
Jon Liu: taking daytime handoff after 12:45 UTC. please add me to INC-1453 and attach /var/log/messages + nvml logs.
Maya Patel: attaching useful logs to the ticket and marking timeline. next steps: driver canary, full metadata collection, and postmortem. good job team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-1453 updated: status=investigating, severity=2, responders=[Maya Patel, Jon Liu, Sophia Ramirez].
Maya Patel: closing pager for now, monitoring at +15/30 intervals. will update once driver canary completes.
